title: Design LTS co-support matrix and automated preflight validator
creator: Liam Chen
description: Create a practical LTS channel design and a cross-surface support matrix (runtime, public API, official SDKs, Console) plus an automated `preflight` validator that gates rollouts. The goal is to make releases predictable for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments while enabling safe, staged upgrades across Hosted API and Console surfaces. Deliverables: a human-readable matrix, machine-readable compatibility rules, and a CLI/CI preflight validator that can run smoke and compatibility checks before canary/GA promotion.
acceptance_criteria: Human-readable matrix mapping LTS channels to supported runtime, API, SDK, and Console versions published to the internal docs site
Machine-readable manifest format (YAML/JSON) describing compatibility rules and allowed coexistence pairs (e.g., runtime X compatible with API Y, SDK Z)

Preflight CLI that performs: semantic API contract checks, SDK compatibility smoke tests (install client, run example requests), runtime KV-cache ABI check, and Console UI compatibility smoke (dashboard load) against a canary cluster
CI integration: preflight job can be added to release pipelines and fails the release when blocked by gating rules
Rollout playbook section describing automated rollback triggers and fast remediation steps when preflight passes but production regressions occur

design_decisions: Decision: Use explicit compatibility matrix (machine-readable) rather than relying solely on semver. Rationale: multiple surfaces (runtime binary, API, SDKs, Console) have different compatibility semantics and release cadences.

Decision: Define 4 compatibility tiers: Fully-compatible (no change), Compatible-with-adapter (requires small adapter shim or config), Non-breaking-contract (minor behavioral differences allowed but gated by tests), Incompatible (requires coordinated rollout and migration plan).
Decision: Preflight validator is composed of modular checks (api-contract, sdk-smoke, runtime-abi, console-ui) so new checks can be added per-surface.

Decision: Default policy for LTS channels: support the runtime and API surfaces for 18 months; SDKs and Console will follow a rolling support window aligned with LTS major with a 12-month minimum. Exceptions can be recorded per-customer for Dedicated/Private.
Decision: Canary rollouts will use smart routing: 5% traffic to new runtime+api, monitor quality/regressions for 48h before automatic progressive ramp. Preflight must pass before initial canary.
Tradeoff noted: Strict backward compatibility reduces product velocity; we will allow adapter layers to keep velocity while guaranteeing customer stability for LTS channels.
implementation_notes: Matrix schema proposal: fields: channel_name, start_date, end_date, min_runtime_version, max_runtime_version, supported_api_versions, supported_sdk_versions, console_compat_flags, special_conditions
Machine manifest format: JSON+schema v1 stored in /infra/releases/lts-manifests/ and also published to internal docs. The validator will pull manifests from a release bucket.
Preflight CLI: `redwood-release-check preflight --manifest <manifest> --target <cluster|canary>` will run checks and emit structured TAP-like output for CI consumption.
Checks implemented so far in PoC: OpenAPI diff against baseline, SDK quick install + generate-token + sample chat request, KV-cache header compatibility introspection against runtime agent endpoint.
Missing work: automated Console dashboard smoke (requires a headless browser job and a stable test dashboard) and enhanced runtime binary compatibility fuzzing.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly conservative matrix blocks harmless releases. Mitigation: provide fast appeal process and an 'adapter' lane for minor incompatibilities.
Risk: Private deployments with pinned components won't be covered by hosted automated remediation. Mitigation: create a documented migration checklist and opt-in upgrade helper for on-prem customers.
Risk: Preflight false negatives due to environment differences. Mitigation: run preflight against multiple representative canary clusters and include feature-flagged checks.
Risk: Matrix maintenance burden. Mitigation: automate manifest generation from release tooling and require a 'compatibility note' in release PRs.
